The Logic Behind It

Every setting here has been refined for V2's smarter chain architecture. Let's break down why this configuration is so different from Plugin #03's voice-track X-Noise.

Threshold: −17.4 (Deeper, More Sensitive Detection)

Compared to the voice-track X-Noise (Threshold: 17.9), this threshold is set dramatically lower — into the negative range. This is intentional:

  • The master chain has compressed the dynamic range considerably, pulling the noise floor closer to the voice level
  • A more sensitive threshold is needed to detect noise that's now riding higher in the spectrum
  • The negative threshold value indicates X-Noise is operating in a fine-detection mode — looking for residual artifacts that survived the entire chain

This is professional-grade calibration — sensitive enough to catch master-chain artifacts, conservative enough to never touch vocal content.

Reduction: 6 (Light, Surgical Subtraction)

Where the voice-track X-Noise used Reduction: 0 (detection-only mode with shelf doing the work), this master pass uses Reduction: 6 — light but actively engaged.

Why the difference?

  • The voice-track X-Noise needed to be completely transparent because compression and saturation came after it
  • This master-bus X-Noise is the last plugin in the chain — there's nothing after it to amplify any artifacts it might create
  • A gentle Reduction of 6 is the perfect amount to scrub residual artifacts without introducing "underwater" coloration
  • This is the safest place in the chain to apply gentle active reduction
iCalibrated Value

Reduction at 6 is the surgical sweet spot for master-bus cleanup. Below 4 leaves audible residue. Above 10 introduces musical noise artifacts on already-mastered content. 6 is precisely calibrated.

High Shelf: 4006 Hz / 0.0 dB (Reserved Slot)

Unlike the voice-track X-Noise which uses the High Shelf actively (at +5.2 dB) to drive the noise reduction work, this master pass keeps the High Shelf at 0 dB (flat).

Why? Because:

  • The master chain has already shaped the top end through Ozone's EQ
  • Adding more high-frequency emphasis here would create double-processing of the already-polished top end
  • The shelf is kept active as a mic-specific corrective slot (see Mic Adaptation Notes)
  • For most users, flat is the correct setting

Attack: 5 / Release: 5 (Identical to First Pass)

Same balanced timing as Plugin #03. These values are universally optimal for X-Noise on dialogue content — there's no reason to change them between instances.

Resolution: Med  ★ (Important Difference From Voice-Track X-Noise)

This is the most important setting on this plugin — and it's deliberately different from Plugin #03.

Plugin #03 (Voice Track) used Low resolution because:

  • Reduction was at 0 (detection-only mode)
  • The signal was raw and dynamically rich
  • Lighter analysis preserved the natural source character

This master-bus X-Noise uses Med resolution because:

  1. Active reduction is occurring (value 6) — Med resolution gives more accurate spectral subtraction
  2. The signal is now polished — minor artifacts are more visible against a clean backdrop, requiring tighter analysis
  3. Master-chain artifacts are spectrally complex — they require finer resolution to identify and remove cleanly
  4. CPU is no longer a concern — this is the last plugin, so we can afford the slightly heavier processing

NR Output: −84.6 (Healthy Operating Range)

This metering value is deeper than the voice-track X-Noise (−65.6) — which makes perfect sense. By this stage of the chain:

  • The noise floor has been dramatically reduced by all upstream processing
  • X-Noise is operating in a much quieter signal environment
  • The deeper NR value confirms the plugin is functioning correctly with very little gain reduction needed

If your NR meter reads significantly higher than this (closer to −40 or −30), you have excessive noise reaching the master bus — investigate upstream plugins.

Monitoring: Audio

Keep set to Audio for normal playback. The Difference mode is your diagnostic tool — switching to it lets you hear only what X-Noise is removing, which is critical for verifying you're not removing voice content (see Pro Tips).

Mic Adaptation Notes

This plugin is less mic-dependent than Plugin #03 because the upstream chain has already normalized differences. However, small adjustments help match different mic outputs:

Low-Self-Noise / Quiet Condenserse.g., Rode NT1-A, Neumann TLM 103, Lewitt LCT 440 Pure
  • Reduce Reduction to 4 — the master chain artifacts are minimal with quiet source mics
  • Keep threshold at default −17.4
Standard Condenserse.g., AKG C214, Audio-Technica AT4040, Sennheiser MK4
  • Use default settings exactly
Warm / Vintage-Voiced Condenserse.g., Neumann U87, Rode NT2-A
  • Use default settings exactly
  • Optionally activate the High Shelf at +1.5 dB if any high-frequency hum survives
Higher-Self-Noise / Budget Condenserse.g., Samson C01, Behringer C-1, AT2020, MXL 990, entry-level USB condensers
  • Increase Reduction to 8 — budget mic noise gets more amplified by the master chain's gain stages
  • Lower threshold to −20.0 for slightly more aggressive detection
  • Optionally activate High Shelf at +2.5 dB / 4006 Hz to target high-frequency hiss common in budget mic capsules
  • ⚠ Don't exceed Reduction 10 — master-bus artifacts become audible faster than voice-track artifacts
Untreated / Semi-Treated Rooms
  • Use defaults — the voice-track X-Noise already handled room noise; this pass focuses on master-chain artifacts
iThe Universal Rule

This plugin's Reduction value should be equal to or slightly higher than the voice-track X-Noise. If you raised the voice-track Reduction to 8 for a budget mic, raise this one to 8–9. Never lower — master-bus cleanup always needs at least equal attention to voice-track cleanup.

Hitting The Sweet Spot

You'll know the master X-Noise is dialed correctly when:

  • Switching to "Difference" monitoring reveals only faint hiss/hum — no recognizable voice content
  • Bypassing reveals a subtle increase in background hiss that wasn't there before mastering
  • Engaging produces no audible change to the voice itself
  • The final master sounds utterly silent in the spaces between words
  • The overall master feels professional, polished, and "expensive"
  • The NR meter sits deep at −80 or lower during normal content
✓The Difference Test

Switch the monitoring mode from Audio to Difference. You should hear only background noise being removed — no recognizable speech, vowels, or consonants. If you hear voice content in Difference mode, your settings are too aggressive — reduce by 2 dB immediately.

✓The Final Listening Test

Export the master. Listen on studio headphones at moderate volume during a silent passage. The silence should sound digitally pristine — no hum, no hiss, no shimmer, no underwater character.

✓The Translation Test

Convert the master to MP3 at 192 kbps and listen on a phone speaker. The silence between words should still be clean and professional. If you hear any artifacts on the lossy version that weren't on the

[Source note: this sentence ends here, mid-thought, in the original guide. Preserved as written.]

Common Mistake
✗Using the same settings as the voice-track X-Noise

Plugin #03 used Resolution: Low + Reduction: 0 + Active High Shelf. Copying those settings here creates audible processing artifacts because this position requires different parameters — Resolution: Med + Reduction: 6 + Flat Shelf. The two instances are designed for fundamentally different jobs.

✗Setting Resolution to "High" thinking it's "the final touch."

High resolution is wrong for master-bus processing on dialogue content. It creates phase issues, transient smearing, and CPU overload — with no audible benefit. Med is the correct, professional choice.

✗Skipping the second profile capture

Loading the same profile from Plugin #03 will fail — the noise spectrum has changed dramatically after mastering. Always capture a fresh profile from the mastered silent section.

✗Pushing Reduction above 10

Beyond 10, this plugin starts removing the natural ambience that gives the master its "live" feel — making the voice sound synthetic, plastic, and over-processed. 6 is the sweet spot. 10 is the absolute ceiling.

✗Forgetting to verify with Difference mode

Without checking Difference mode before finalizing, you can't know if you're removing voice content. Always verify before bouncing the master.

✗Disabling this plugin "because the master sounds clean enough."

The master may sound clean on studio monitors — but on phone speakers, in cars, and through MP3 codecs, the artifacts this plugin removes become audible. Always keep this plugin engaged for delivery-grade masters.
